document_summary: Official LAHD page giving the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) annual allowable rent increase (3% for July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026), a rent increase calculator, and notes on the end of the utility add-on and on surcharge pass-throughs.

rules.title: Los Angeles RSO annual allowable rent increase
rules.requirement: Landlords of RSO units may raise rent by no more than the annual allowable percentage (3% for July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026). Beginning February 2, 2026, no additional percentage for utilities may be added.
rules.key_value: 3% annual allowable increase (7/1/2025-6/30/2026); no additional utilities percentage beginning 2026-02-02
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental units subject to the City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO); check status at zimas.lacity.org.
rules.exemptions: Non-RSO properties are not covered by this figure; the page refers them to LAHD for allowable increases.
rules.interaction: State law requires 30 days' written advance notice of rent increases of less than 10%. RSO and SCEP surcharges ($1.61 and $2.83 per month) may be passed through with written notice, separate from the rent increase.
rules.citation: L.A.M.C. § 151.06 (Rent Stabilization Ordinance, annual allowable rent increase)
rules.quoted_span: Annual rent increases for rental units subject to the City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO), effective July 1, 2025, through June 30, 2026 is 3% . Beginning February 2, 2026, a landlord can no longer include any additional percentage increase for utilities.
rules.conflict_note: Los Angeles's new RSO formula has two published effective dates: 2026-02-02 per LAHD and 2026-01-24 per a landlord association. This LAHD page states February 2, 2026 for the end of the utilities add-on; the landlord-association 2026-01-24 date is not found in this capture. The page also shows only the 2025-26 3% figure, not a figure for the new formula.
rules.extraction_notes: Effective date is taken from the page's 'Beginning February 2, 2026' statement about the utilities add-on, which is a change to the increase formula. The 3% figure applies to the period July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026 and the page does not give a later-year figure. The citation is inferred from general knowledge; the page does not cite code sections. This is an official city page, not the ordinance text.
